Therefore at the opening of this chapter the Apostle rules out their evil suspicion, saying: [[3:1|Do we begin again|Incipimus iterum]] in this epistle, as in the first, [[3:1|to commend|commendare]], that is, to praise, [[3:1|ourselves|nos ipsos]], namely for our own glory, and not rather for the glory of God, for your instruction, so that, knowing the truth, you may believe us and not the false apostles? [[3:1|Or do we need|Aut numquid egemus]], [[3:1|as some do|sicut quidam]], deceivers and hypocrites, [[3:1|epistles of commendation|commendaticiis, id est laudatoriis, epistolis]] (that is, letters of praise) to be sent [[3:1|to you, or from you|ad vos, aut ex vobis]], that is, to be sent on by you to others? As if to say: On our own account we have no need at all of such letters, since our own virtue commends us enough; yet for the sake of the ignorant they are necessary, lest they be deceived.

paras.t: Quod autem non indigemus commendaticiis litteris, patet : nam, Epistola nostra, id est, aliquid simile epistolæ nostræ, videlicet conversi ac instituti a nobis, vos estis, quia in vobis nostra virtus et sapientia declarantur quasi in libro : epistola, inquam, scripta, id est vehementer impressa, in cordibus nostris, quoniam indesinenter memoriam sollicitudinemque pro vestra salute habemus; quæ epistola scitur et legitur ab omnibus hominibus, id est, cunctis fidelibus constat vos esse conversos et institutos a nobis. Legunt quoque et discunt seu pensant in vobis, vel ex vestræ conversationis intuitu, quales nos simus, sicut ex consideratione discipuli innotescit prudentia perfectioque magistri.
paras.en: That we do not need letters of commendation is plain: for [[3:2|our epistle|Epistola nostra]], that is, something like a letter of ours, namely men converted and taught by us, [[3:2|You are|vos estis]], because in you our virtue and wisdom are set forth as in a book: an epistle, I say, [[3:2|written|scripta]], that is, deeply impressed, [[3:2|in our hearts|in cordibus nostris]], since we keep you unceasingly in mind and in our care for your salvation; [[3:2|which is known and read by all men|quæ epistola scitur et legitur ab omnibus hominibus]]: that is, all the faithful know that you were converted and taught by us. They also read and learn, or weigh, in you, or from beholding your way of life, what manner of men we are, just as the prudence and perfection of a master become known from considering his disciple.

paras.t: Manifestati, id est, per fidem et opera bona hoc aliis de vobis ostensum est, quoniam epistola estis Christi, id est a Christo principaliter instituti et scripti, cujus etiam virtus et gratia in vobis repræsentatur, ministrata a nobis, id est, nostro ministerio ad fidem deducti et Christo exhibiti estis : epistola, inquam, scripta non atramento, quomodo scripsit Baruch ex ore Jeremiæ, sed Spiritu Dei vivi, id est Spiritu Sancto, a quo instituti estis et inter electos adscripti. Ipse enim est digitus Dei, quo divina in nobis scribuntur seu imprimuntur. De quo loquitur Christus : Si in digito Dei ejicio dæmonia, etc. Scripti autem non in tabulis lapideis, quomodo scripta erat lex Moysis, id est non instituti in cordibus duris, nec hujusmodi cordibus impressi, sed in tabulis cordis carnalibus, id est in cordibus piis ac mollibus, vel in intellectu prudenti, voluntate benigna, memoria stabili. De quibus tabulis legitur in Proverbiis : Serva mandata et legem quasi pupillam oculi tui, et in tabulis cordis tui scribe ea. In talibus ergo tabulis fideles scripti dicuntur a Spiritu Sancto : Primo, quia per ejus institutionem et gratiam corda habent hujusmodi : lata, scilicet per caritatem; aperta, per obedientialem promptitudinem; plena, per mansuetudinem; mollia, per divini verbi celerem receptionem et compunctionem. Unde Dominus per Ezechielem promittit : Auferam cor lapideum de carne vestra, et dabo vobis cor carneum, et spiritum novum ponam in medio vestri. Secundo, quia piis fidelibusque prælatis ac proximis impressit Spiritus Sanctus curam de salute aliorum.
paras.en: [[3:3|Being manifested|Manifestati]], that is, this has been shown to others concerning you through faith and good works, [[3:3|that you are the epistle of Christ|quoniam epistola estis Christi]], that is, taught and written principally by Christ, whose virtue and grace are also shown forth in you, [[3:3|ministered by us|ministrata a nobis]], that is, by our ministry you were led to the faith and presented to Christ: an epistle, I say, [[3:3|written|scripta]] [[3:3|not with ink|non atramento]], as Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremias[[Jer 36:18||]], [[3:3|but with the Spirit of the living God|sed Spiritu Dei vivi]], that is, with the Holy Spirit, by whom you were taught and enrolled among the elect. For he is the finger of God, by which divine things are written or impressed in us. Of him Christ speaks: [[Luke 11:20|if I by the finger of God cast out devils|Si in digito Dei ejicio dæmonia]], etc. Written, moreover, [[3:3|not in tables of stone|non in tabulis lapideis]], as the law of Moses was written[[Ex 34:4||]][[Ex 34:28||]], that is, not taught in hard hearts, nor impressed on such hearts, [[3:3|but in the fleshly tables of the heart|sed in tabulis cordis carnalibus]], that is, in loving and tender hearts, or in a prudent understanding, a kindly will and a steadfast memory. Of these tables we read in Proverbs: [[Prov 7:2|Keep my commandments|Serva mandata]], [[Prov 7:2|and my law as the apple of thy eye|et legem quasi pupillam oculi tui]], and [[Prov 7:3|write it upon the tables of thy heart|tabulis cordis tui scribe ea]]. In such tables, then, the faithful are said to be written by the Holy Spirit: first, because by his teaching and grace they have hearts of this kind: broad, namely through charity; open, through the readiness of obedience; full, through meekness; tender, through the swift reception of the divine word, and through compunction. Hence the Lord promises through Ezechiel: [[Ezech 36:26|I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and will give you a heart of flesh|Auferam cor lapideum de carne vestra, et dabo vobis cor carneum]], [[Ezech 36:26|and put a new spirit within you|et spiritum novum ponam in medio vestri]]. Second, because the Holy Spirit has impressed on loving and faithful prelates, and on our neighbours, a care for the salvation of others.

paras.t: Præterea declarat Apostolus, quod non proprie commendet se ipsum, sed Deum, quum omne bonum ei adscribat. Fiduciam autem talem, id est audaciam sic loquendi de nostris præconiis, habemus per Christum, id est a Christo per gratiam ejus, ad Deum Trinitatem, coram quo ista fiducialiter dicimus. Non quod sufficientes simus cogitare, et per consequens nec dicere, nec facere possumus, aliquid meritorium a nobis, id est propria potestate, quasi ex nobis, id est tanquam ex prima et principali virtute. Licet enim nos simus causa operis boni per liberum arbitrium, quia nec aliter meremur, natura tamen nostra indiget gratia : nam liberum arbitrium indiget non solum habitu gratiæ supernaturalis et divinæ dilectionis, sed etiam actuali motione Spiritus Sancti nos excitantis. In quo damnatur error Pelagii, asserentis quod inchoatio operum meritoriorum sit a nobis, consummatio vero a Deo. Inchoatio enim in nobis, est cogitatio, in qua operatur Deus, secundum Apostolum. Unde alibi loquitur : Deus operatur in nobis velle et perficere. Ideo subditur : sed sufficientia nostra, id est virtus et efficacia meritorie cogitandi, loquendi ac operandi, ex Deo est, id est ex motione et gratia Dei, a quo est omne datum optimum et donum perfectum. Propter quod ait Salvator : Sine me nihil potestis facere ; et per Prophetam : Perditio tua, Israel, ex te ; in me tantummodo auxilium tuum.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle declares that he is not, properly speaking, commending himself but God, since he ascribes every good to him. [[3:4|And such confidence|Fiduciam autem talem]], that is, boldness to speak thus of our praises, [[3:4|we have, through Christ|habemus per Christum]], that is, from Christ through his grace, [[3:4|towards God|ad Deum]] the Trinity, before whom we say these things confidently. [[3:5|Not that we are sufficient to think|Non quod sufficientes simus cogitare]] (and consequently we can neither speak nor do) [[3:5|any thing|aliquid]] meritorious [[3:5|of ourselves|a nobis]], that is, by our own power, [[3:5|as of ourselves|quasi ex nobis]], that is, as from the first and principal power. For although we are the cause of a good work through free will (since otherwise we would not merit), yet our nature needs grace: for free will needs not only the habit of supernatural grace and of divine love, but also the actual motion [that is, a present impulse to act, as distinct from an abiding habit] of the Holy Spirit stirring us up. Herein is condemned the error of Pelagius, who asserted that the beginning of meritorious works is from us, but their completion from God. For the beginning in us is thought, and in it God works, according to the Apostle. Hence he says elsewhere: [[Phil 2:13|God who worketh in you, both to will and to accomplish|Deus operatur in nobis velle et perficere]] [Denis reads *in nobis*, in us]. Therefore it is added: [[3:5|but our sufficiency|sed sufficientia nostra]], that is, the power and efficacy of thinking, speaking and working meritoriously, [[3:5|is from God|ex Deo est]], that is, from the motion and grace of God, from whom is [[Jas 1:17|Every best gift and every perfect gift|omne datum optimum et donum perfectum]]. For this reason the Saviour says: [[John 15:5|without me you can do nothing|Sine me nihil potestis facere]]; and through the Prophet: [[Osee 13:9|Destruction is thy own, O Israel: thy help is only in me.|Perditio tua, Israel, ex te ; in me tantummodo auxilium tuum]]

paras.t: Qui et idoneos nos fecit ministros, id est efficaces et dignos prædicatores, novi Testamenti, id est evangelicæ legis ; non littera, id est non instructione litterali, sed spiritu, id est illustratione Spiritus Sancti, a quo vitam et sapientiam nos ad tantum officium dignificantem accepimus. Novum quippe Testamentum non est datum Apostolis per exteriorem scripturam, sed per internam illustrationem. Ideo vocatur lex spiritus. Lex autem Mosaica appellatur lex litteræ, quia in libro ac tabulis scripta. Ad cujus distinctionis insinuationem Dominus ait per Jeremiam : Ecce dies veniunt, et feriam domui Israel et domui Juda pactum novum, non tale quale pepigi cum patribus eorum, etc. Ratio autem cur Deus nos fecit idoneos non littera sed spiritu, est : Littera enim, id est lex scripta, occidit ex occasione, quia non contulit gratiam, et auxit concupiscentiam, eo quod homo nitatur in vetitum ; auxit quoque generaliter culpam, quoniam post veritatis notitiam gravius est peccare quam ante ; Spiritus autem Sanctus, qui per Apostolorum ministrationem dabatur fidelibus, et nunc per sacramenta Ecclesiæ datur hominibus, vivificat vita gratiæ corda credentium. Vel sic : Littera, id est sensus literalis, vel potius qui literalis videtur, occidit ; spiritus autem, id est intellectus spiritualis ac mysticus, vivificat.
paras.en: [[3:6|Who also hath made us fit ministers|Qui et idoneos nos fecit ministros]], that is, effective and worthy preachers, [[3:6|of the new testament|novi Testamenti]], that is, of the gospel law; [[3:6|not in the letter|non littera]], that is, not by instruction in letters, [[3:6|but in the spirit|sed spiritu]], that is, by the enlightening of the Holy Spirit, from whom we have received the life and wisdom that make us worthy of so great an office. For the New Testament was not given to the Apostles by outward writing, but by inward enlightenment; therefore it is called the law of the spirit. The Mosaic law, on the other hand, is called the law of the letter, because it was written in a book and on tables. To point to this distinction the Lord says through Jeremias: [[Jer 31:31|Behold the days shall come|Ecce dies veniunt]], [[Jer 31:31|and I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Juda|et feriam domui Israel et domui Juda pactum novum]], [[Jer 31:32|Not according to the covenant which I made with their fathers|non tale quale pepigi cum patribus eorum]], etc. Now the reason why God made us fit not in the letter but in the spirit is this: [[3:6|For the letter|Littera enim]], that is, the written law, [[3:6|killeth|occidit]] by occasion [that is, not of itself but as the occasion of sin], because it did not confer grace and it increased concupiscence, since man strives after what is forbidden; it also increased guilt generally, since after the truth is known it is more grievous to sin than before; [[3:6|but the spirit|Spiritus autem]], the Holy Spirit, who was given to the faithful through the ministry of the Apostles, and is now given to men through the sacraments of the Church, [[3:6|quickeneth|vivificat]] the hearts of believers with the life of grace. Or thus: [[3:6|the letter|Littera]], that is, the literal sense, or rather what seems to be the literal sense, [[3:6|killeth|occidit]]; [[3:6|but the spirit|spiritus autem]], that is, the spiritual and mystical understanding, [[3:6|quickeneth|vivificat]].

paras.t: Proinde ostendit Apostolus dignitatem ministrorum novi Testamenti, comparatione ministrorum veteris Testamenti. Quod si, id est Quia, ministratio mortis, id est exhibitio instrumentalis veteris legis, per occasionem occidentis animam transgressoris (ut dictum est sæpius : virtus enim peccati lex), et etiam mortem corporalem facile inferentis, litteris visibilibus deformata, id est scripta, in lapidibus, id est lapideis tabulis, fuit in gloria, id est, gloriam habuit in suo ministro, seu ministeriali legislatore, ita ut non possent filii Israel intendere, id est visum figere, in faciem Moysis propter gloriam, id est claritatem, vultus ejus : in quo apparuerunt radii splendidi, angulariter ascendentes in similitudine cornuum, repercutientes intuitum filiorum Israel : unde et facies ejus dicitur fuisse cornuta ; quæ evacuatur, id est, quæ claritas Moysis, vel quæ ministratio finitur et cessat. Cito enim desiit claritas illa ; vetus quoque lex cessavit, nova lege promulgata. Quomodo non magis ministratio Spiritus, id est evangelicæ legis gratiam Sancti Spiritus ratione sacramentorum continentis, erit in gloria, id est, dignitatem et gloriam habebit in suis ministris, puta Apostolis, in præsenti atque futuro, etiam ampliorem quam ministratio mortis? quasi dicat, Imo habebit.
paras.en: Next the Apostle shows the dignity of the ministers of the New Testament by comparing them with the ministers of the Old. [[3:7|Now if|Quod si]], that is, Since, [[3:7|the ministration of death|ministratio mortis]], that is, the instrumental presentation of the old law, which by occasion kills the soul of the transgressor (as has often been said: for [[1 Cor 15:56|the power of sin is the law|virtus enim peccati lex]]), and which also readily inflicted bodily death, [[3:7|engraven with letters|litteris visibilibus deformata]] [Denis reads *litteris visibilibus deformata*, engraven with visible letters], that is, written, [[3:7|upon stones|in lapidibus]], that is, on tables of stone, [[3:7|was glorious|fuit in gloria]], that is, had glory in its minister, or ministering lawgiver, [[3:7|so that the children of Israel could not steadfastly behold|ita ut non possent filii Israel intendere]], that is, fix their gaze upon, [[3:7|the face of Moses|in faciem Moysis]], [[3:7|for the glory|propter gloriam]], that is, the brightness, [[3:7|of his countenance|vultus ejus]]: in which there appeared shining rays, rising at angles in the likeness of horns and striking back the gaze of the children of Israel; whence his face also is said to have been horned[[Ex 34:30||]] [the margin gives Exod. xxxiv, 33; the horned face is told at Ex 34:29–30, the veil at 34:33]; [[3:7|which is made void|quæ evacuatur]], that is, which brightness of Moses, or which ministration, comes to an end and ceases. For that brightness soon passed away; and the old law also ceased when the new law was promulgated. [[3:8|How shall not the ministration of the spirit|Quomodo non magis ministratio Spiritus]], that is, of the gospel law, which contains the grace of the Holy Spirit by reason of the sacraments, [[3:8|be rather in glory|erit in gloria]], that is, have dignity and glory in its ministers, for instance the Apostles, in the present and in the future, and greater even than the ministration of death? As if to say: Indeed it shall.

paras.t: Ideo subditur : Nam si ministratio damnationis, id est veteris legis, damnationem æternam accidenter augentis et inferentis, quoniam peccatum prohibendo, nec tamen gratiam largiendo, auxit peccatum, sicque damnationi fecit obnoxium. Sicut enim occidit, ita et damnavit. De cujus rei intellectu tractatum est plenius ad Romanos. Si ergo ministratio ista gloria est, id est honor et dignitas Moysis ; […] ministerium justitiæ, id est ministratio novæ legis, veram perfectionem et gratiam juste vivendi includentis, in gloria, id est, copiosiorem gloriam habet annexam. Ecce quomodo sanctus Apostolus se ipsum et compostolos suos Moysi præfert, saltem quantum ad gratias gratis datas.
paras.en: Therefore it is added: [[3:9|For if the ministration of condemnation|Nam si ministratio damnationis]], that is, of the old law, which accidentally increased and brought on eternal damnation, since by forbidding sin, and yet not bestowing grace, it increased sin, and so made man liable to damnation. For as it killed, so also it condemned. The understanding of this was treated more fully in Romans. If, then, this ministration [[3:9|be glory|gloria est]], that is, the honour and dignity of Moses, […] [[3:9|the ministration of justice|ministerium justitiæ]], that is, the ministration of the new law, which includes true perfection and the grace of living justly, [[3:9|in glory|in gloria]], that is, has a more abundant glory joined to it. See how the holy Apostle sets himself and his fellow apostles above Moses, at least as regards the graces freely given [*gratiæ gratis datæ*: gifts such as prophecy, tongues and miracles, given for the good of others rather than to make holy the one who receives them].

paras.t: Nam nec glorificatum est, id est, gloriosum reputandum non est, quod claruit in hac parte, id est lumen vultus Moysis, propter excellentem gloriam, id est propter vehementem excessum dignitatis et gloriæ ministris novi Testamenti concessum, quæ tanta est, ut comparatione ejus, gloria vultus Moysis quasi nihil sit. Vel sic : Nam nec glorificatum est, id est, hominibus perfecte revelari non potuit, quod claruit in hac parte, id est gloria ministris novæ legis collata. Tanta est enim gloria et dignitas Apostolorum, ut viatores capere nequeant.
paras.en: For [[3:10|was not glorified|nec glorificatum est]], that is, is not to be reckoned glorious, [[3:10|that which was glorious in this part|quod claruit in hac parte]], that is, the light of Moses' face, [[3:10|by reason of the glory that excelleth|propter excellentem gloriam]], that is, on account of the overwhelming excess of dignity and glory granted to the ministers of the New Testament, which is so great that in comparison with it the glory of Moses' face is as nothing. Or thus: For [[3:10|was not glorified|nec glorificatum est]], that is, could not be perfectly revealed to men, [[3:10|that which was glorious in this part|quod claruit in hac parte]], that is, the glory bestowed on the ministers of the new law. For so great is the glory and dignity of the Apostles that wayfarers [*viatores*, men still on their way in this life] cannot grasp it.

paras.t: Porro quod subditur, utique consonat expositioni. Si enim quod evacuatur, id est vetus Testamentum quod cessavit, per gloriam est, id est, per gloriam et claritatem Moysis præstitum, datum ac receptum est; multo magis quod manet, id est nova lex, cui alia non succedet danda a Deo, in gloria est, id est, dignitatem gloriosam habet annexam.
paras.en: What follows, moreover, agrees with this exposition. [[3:11|For if that which is done away|Si enim quod evacuatur]], that is, the Old Testament, which has ceased, [[3:11|was glorious|per gloriam est]], that is, was furnished, given and received through the glory and brightness of Moses; [[3:11|much more that which remaineth|multo magis quod manet]], that is, the new law, which no other law to be given by God shall succeed, [[3:11|is in glory|in gloria est]], that is, has a glorious dignity joined to it.

paras.t: Habentes igitur talem spem, videlicet quod tanta nobis collata est gratia, et tanta gloria præparata, multa fiducia utimur, id est, cum ingenti confidentia nostrum officium exercemus, certi de gloria remunerationis, et non celamus mysteria Scripturarum, seu mysticos sensus.
paras.en: [[3:12|Having therefore such hope|Habentes igitur talem spem]], namely that so great a grace has been bestowed on us and so great a glory prepared, [[3:12|we use much confidence|multa fiducia utimur]], that is, we carry out our office with great confidence, sure of the glory of the reward, and we do not hide the mysteries of the Scriptures, that is, their mystical senses.

paras.t: Et non sicut Moyses ponebat velamen, id est pannum quemdam seu operimentum, super faciem suam cornutam seu lucidam ex colloquio Dei, ut non intenderent filii Israel in faciem ejus, quia nec eam inspicere poterant præ splendore, nisi esset velo obducta. Per quod figurabatur, quod spiritualis et verus intellectus veteris Testamenti tegebatur obscuritatibus figurarum legalium. Quod velamen evacuatur, id est, per doctrinam Apostolorum atque doctorum aufertur, dum veteris Testamenti Scriptura vere elucidatur.
paras.en: [[3:13|And not as Moses put a veil|Et non sicut Moyses ponebat velamen]], that is, a kind of cloth or covering, [[3:13|upon his face|super faciem suam]], which was horned, or shining, from his speaking with God, [[3:13|that the children of Israel might not steadfastly look on the face|ut non intenderent filii Israel in faciem ejus]], for they could not even look at it for its splendour, unless it was covered with the veil. By this it was signified that the spiritual and true understanding of the Old Testament was covered by the obscurities of the figures of the law. Which veil [[3:13|is made void|evacuatur]], that is, is taken away by the teaching of the Apostles and doctors, when the Scripture of the Old Testament is truly explained.

paras.t: Sed obtusi, id est excæcati, sunt sensus eorum, id est mentales oculi infidelium Judæorum : juxta illud, Obscurentur oculi eorum ne videant. Usque in hodiernum enim diem id ipsum velamen, id est figuralis obscuritas legis, in lectione veteris Testamenti, id est, dum legitur Scriptura veteris Testamenti, Judæis manet non revelatum, id est occulta seu non intellecta, quia non aliter intelligunt Scripturas legis veteris modo, quam ante. Ideo velamen non est amotum a corde eorum : quamvis a re ipsa amotum sit. Unde subditur : quoniam in Christo evacuatur, id est, per fidem et doctrinam Christi amovetur, et veritas Scripturarum ostenditur. In cujus figura, tempore dominicæ passionis velum templi est scissum a summo usque deorsum. Per Christi etenim passionem revelantur legis ac Prophetarum sacramenta. Velamen itaque appellatur opertio prophetiæ, quæ in Christo impletur. Sed usque in hodiernum diem, id est tempus gratiæ, quum legitur Moyses, id est Pentateuchus, videlicet Scriptura quinque librorum Moysis, velamen, id est cæcitas seu opertio ista, est positum super cor eorum, id est infidelium Judæorum.
paras.en: [[3:14|But their senses were made dull|sed obtusi sunt sensus eorum]]: *made dull*, that is, blinded; *their senses*, that is, the mental eyes of the unbelieving Jews; according to that: [[Ps 68:24|Let their eyes be darkened that they see not|Obscurentur oculi eorum ne videant]]. [[3:14|For, until this present day|Usque in hodiernum enim diem]] [[3:14|the selfsame veil|id ipsum velamen]], that is, the figurative obscurity of the law, [[3:14|in the reading of the old testament|in lectione veteris Testamenti]], that is, while the Scripture of the Old Testament is read, [[3:14|remaineth not taken away|manet non revelatum]] for the Jews, that is, hidden or not understood, because they understand the Scriptures of the old law no otherwise now than before. So the veil has not been removed from their heart, although it has been removed in the thing itself. Hence it is added: [[3:14|because in Christ it is made void|quoniam in Christo evacuatur]], that is, it is removed by the faith and teaching of Christ, and the truth of the Scriptures is shown. In figure of this, at the time of the Lord's passion, [[Matt 27:51|the veil of the temple was rent in two from the top even to the bottom|velum templi est scissum a summo usque deorsum]]. For by Christ's passion the sacraments [that is, the hidden mysteries] of the law and of the Prophets are revealed. So the veil is the name for the covering of prophecy, which is fulfilled in Christ. [[3:15|But even until this day|Sed usque in hodiernum diem]], that is, the time of grace, [[3:15|when Moses is read|quum legitur Moyses]], that is, the Pentateuch, namely the Scripture of the five books of Moses, [[3:15|the veil|velamen]], that is, this blindness or covering, [[3:15|is upon their heart|est positum super cor eorum]], that is, the heart of the unbelieving Jews.

paras.t: Quum autem conversi fuerint ad Dominum, recipiendo fidem catholicam, auferetur velamen prædictum a corde eorum : imo ista conversio aliquid aliud non videtur, nisi velaminis hujus ablatio. Tunc enim illuminabuntur corda ipsorum, juxta illud propheticum : Post hæc revertentur filii Israel, et quærent Dominum Deum suum, et David regem suum, id est Messiam, sicut Judæi quoque exponunt.
paras.en: [[3:16|But when they shall be converted to the Lord|Quum autem conversi fuerint ad Dominum]], by receiving the Catholic faith, [[3:16|the veil shall be taken away|auferetur velamen]], the veil spoken of, from their heart: indeed, this conversion seems to be nothing else than the taking away of this veil. For then their hearts will be enlightened, according to that prophetic word: [[Osee 3:5|after this the children of Israel shall return and shall seek the Lord, their God, and David, their king|Post hæc revertentur filii Israel, et quærent Dominum Deum suum, et David regem suum]], that is, the Messias, as the Jews too expound it.

paras.t: Denique, quod per Spiritum Sanctum auferatur velamen, declarat. Dominus autem Spiritus est. Quamvis hoc de Deo Trinitate verum sit, juxta illud, Spiritus est Deus ; jam tamen de Spiritu Sancto asseritur, qui quum sit Dominus, omnia agit quæ vult, et quomodo vult, sicut superius dictum est : Hæc omnia operatur unus atque idem Spiritus, dividens singulis prout vult. Illuminat ergo quos vult, et derelinquit quos vult, sicut legitur : Spiritus ubi vult, spirat. Ubi autem est Spiritus Domini, id est in mente quam per gratiam Spiritus Sanctus inhabitat, ibi libertas dilectionis, non coactio timoris, libera vacatio animi a jugo diaboli et a servitute peccati, ad contemplandum, diligendum ac operandum ea quæ Dei sunt. Infidelibus itaque inest velamen.
paras.en: Lastly he declares that the veil is taken away by the Holy Spirit: [[3:17|Now the Lord is a Spirit|Dominus autem Spiritus est]]. Although this is true of God the Trinity, according to that: [[John 4:24|God is a spirit|Spiritus est Deus]]; yet here it is asserted of the Holy Spirit, who, since he is Lord, does all that he wills and as he wills, as was said above: [[1 Cor 12:11|all these things, one and the same Spirit worketh, dividing to every one according as he will|Hæc omnia operatur unus atque idem Spiritus, dividens singulis prout vult]]. He enlightens, then, whom he wills, and leaves whom he wills, as we read: [[John 3:8|The Spirit breatheth where he will|Spiritus ubi vult, spirat]]. [[3:17|And where the Spirit of the Lord is|Ubi autem est Spiritus Domini]], that is, in the mind which the Holy Spirit dwells in by grace, [[3:17|there is liberty|ibi libertas]] of love, not the compulsion of fear: the soul's free release from the yoke of the devil and from the servitude of sin, for contemplating, loving and doing the things that are God's. In unbelievers, therefore, the veil remains.

paras.t: Nos vero omnes, id est fideles, præsertim Apostoli et viri perfecti, revelata facie interiori, id est intellectu a prædicto velamine liberato, gloriam Domini, id est majestatem divinam, seu Dominum gloriosum, vel Filium Dei Patris (de quo Isaias, Revelabitur, inquit, gloria Domini : siquidem filius sapiens, gloria patris est), speculantes nunc per fidem et per speculum in ænigmate ; in eamdem imaginem, id est divinæ majestatis seu Filii Dei quamdam deiformem assimilationem, transformamur : quia cognitio fit per assimilationem cognoscentis ad cognitum, secundum Boetium. Ideo contemplator divinorum, divinus seu deiformis efficitur.
paras.en: [[3:18|But we all|Nos vero omnes]], that is, the faithful, especially the Apostles and perfect men, [[3:18|with open face|revelata facie]], the inward face, that is, with the understanding freed from the veil spoken of, [[3:18|the glory of the Lord|gloriam Domini]], that is, the divine majesty, or the glorious Lord, or the Son of God the Father (of whom Isaias: [[Is 40:5|shall be revealed|Revelabitur]], he says, [[Is 40:5|the glory of the Lord|gloria Domini]]; for a wise son is the glory of his father[[Prov 10:1||]] [the margin gives Prov. x, 1, where the Douay-Rheims has: A wise son maketh the father glad]), [[3:18|beholding|speculantes]] now by faith and [[1 Cor 13:12|through a glass in a dark manner|per speculum in ænigmate]] [*speculantes*, beholding, comes from *speculum*, a glass or mirror]; [[3:18|into the same image|in eamdem imaginem]], that is, into a certain deiform likeness to the divine majesty, or to the Son of God, [[3:18|are transformed|transformamur]]: because knowledge comes about through the likening of the knower to the known, according to Boethius. Therefore the contemplator of divine things is made divine, or deiform.

paras.t: Transformamur autem, id est, salubriter commutamur, a claritate luminis naturalis, in claritatem luminis gratiæ, et a claritate viæ seu gratiæ, in claritatem patriæ et gloriæ. Vel sic, et melius, ut opinor : A claritate in claritatem, id est de gratia minori in gratiam ampliorem, proficiendo in bonis et proficiscendo de virtutibus in virtutes. Quanto enim divinorum contemplationi magis insistimus, tanto exuberantiori lumine cœlestis gratiæ perfundimur atque implemur ; et transformamur, id est, a forma seu modo propriæ subsistentiæ transferimur ad divinæ naturæ seu formæ modum ac imitationem. Imo unum cum Deo per caritatem efficimur, angelicam et divinam in hoc exsilio conversationem inchoantes. Et omnia hæc nobis insunt et competunt, non a nobis, sed tanquam a Domini Spiritu, id est virtute et gratia Spiritus Sancti, sicut alibi dictum est : Spiritus adjuvat infirmitatem nostram.
paras.en: We [[3:18|are transformed|Transformamur]], moreover, that is, are changed unto salvation, from the brightness [*claritas*, the word the Douay-Rheims renders glory] of the light of nature into the brightness of the light of grace, and from the brightness of the way, that is, of grace, into the brightness of the fatherland and of glory. Or thus, and better, I think: [[3:18|from glory to glory|A claritate in claritatem]], that is, from lesser grace into greater, by advancing in good things and going on from virtue to virtue[[Ps 83:8||]]. For the more we apply ourselves to the contemplation of divine things, the more abundant is the light of heavenly grace with which we are flooded and filled; and we [[3:18|are transformed|transformamur]], that is, we are carried over from the form or mode of our own subsistence to the mode and imitation of the divine nature or form. Indeed, we are made one with God by charity, beginning in this exile an angelic and divine way of life. And all these things are in us and belong to us not from ourselves, but [[3:18|as by the Spirit of the Lord|tanquam a Domini Spiritu]], that is, by the power and grace of the Holy Spirit, as was said elsewhere: [[Rom 8:26|the Spirit also helpeth our infirmity|Spiritus adjuvat infirmitatem nostram]].

4.title: Elucidatio capituli quarti: Ideo habentes hanc administrationem
4.title_en: Explanation of the fourth chapter: Therefore, seeing we have this ministration

paras.t: Laudavit se sanctus Apostolus ad gloriam Dei et ædificationem audientium, in præcedenti capitulo, ratione dignitatis ministerii sibi commissi; nunc idem facit ex debito usu obsequii sui, ostendens se fructuose et optime usum gratia sibi concessa.
paras.en: In the preceding chapter the holy Apostle praised himself, to the glory of God and the edification of his hearers, by reason of the dignity of the ministry committed to him; now he does the same on the ground of the due use of his service, showing that he has used the grace granted him fruitfully and in the best way.

paras.t: Ideo, id est, quoniam tantam claritatem a Spiritu Sancto suscepimus, habentes hanc administrationem novæ legis, videlicet apostolatum seu ministerium tantæ dignitatis, juxta quod misericordiam consecuti sumus, id est secundum mensuram divinæ pietatis nobis impensæ, non deficimus in adversis, nec ab executione nostri cessamus officii, sed abdicamus, id est abjicimus, occulta dedecoris, id est vitia latentia, quæ non decent, sed deformant et indecorant: non ambulantes in astutia, id est, non dolose aut simulatorie conversantes sicut hypocritæ. Simulatores namque et callidi provocant iram Dei. Astutia autem quandoque in bono accipitur, pro quadam circumspectione, sicut in Proverbiis legitur: Astutus considerat gressus suos. Nunc vero pro versutia sumitur. Unde Salomon: Vir, inquit, versutus odiosus est. Neque adulterantes, id est, perverse interpretantes, seu admiscentes falsitatibus, verbum Dei, videlicet Evangelium Christi; sed in manifestatione veritatis conversamur, id est, ipsam veritatem publice prædicamus et clare exponimus, commendantes, id est commendabiles seu laude dignos facientes, nosmetipsos, recte docendo et bene agendo, ad omnem conscientiam hominum, id est testimonia conscientiarum, vel in conscientiis hominum, ita ut nemo bona conscientia vituperare nos poterit. Et hoc facimus coram Deo, id est divinam præsentiam cogitando, nosque in Dei cuncta cernentis conspectu ponendo, cum omni reverentia atque custodia cordis.
paras.en: [[4:1|Therefore|Ideo]], that is, since we have received so great a brightness from the Holy Ghost, [[4:1|seeing we have this ministration|habentes hanc administrationem]] of the new law, namely the apostleship or ministry of such great dignity, [[4:1|according as we have obtained mercy|juxta quod misericordiam consecuti sumus]], that is, according to the measure of the divine kindness bestowed on us, [[4:1|we faint not|non deficimus]] in adversity, nor do we cease from carrying out our office, [[4:2|But we renounce|sed abdicamus]], that is, we cast away, [[4:2|the hidden things of dishonesty|occulta dedecoris]], that is, hidden vices, which are not becoming but deform and dishonour: [[4:2|not walking in craftiness|non ambulantes in astutia]], that is, not behaving deceitfully or feignedly, like hypocrites. For [[Job 36:13|Dissemblers and crafty men prove the wrath of God|Simulatores namque et callidi provocant iram Dei]]. Now *craftiness* [Latin *astutia*, which can mean shrewdness as well as cunning] is sometimes taken in a good sense, for a certain circumspection, as we read in Proverbs: [[Prov 14:15|the discreet man considereth his steps|Astutus considerat gressus suos]] [Latin *astutus*, the same word]. But here it is taken for cunning. Hence Solomon: [[Prov 14:17|the crafty man|Vir]], he says, [[Prov 14:17|is hateful|versutus odiosus est]] [no margin reference here; the words are Prov 14:17]. [[4:2|nor adulterating|Neque adulterantes]], that is, interpreting perversely, or mixing with falsehoods, [[4:2|the word of God|verbum Dei]], namely the Gospel of Christ; [[4:2|but by manifestation of the truth|sed in manifestatione veritatis]] we behave [Denis adds *conversamur*, "we behave"], that is, we preach the truth itself publicly and expound it clearly, [[4:2|commending|commendantes]], that is, making commendable or worthy of praise, [[4:2|ourselves|nosmetipsos]], by teaching rightly and acting well, [[4:2|to every man's conscience|ad omnem conscientiam hominum]], that is, to the testimony of consciences, or in the consciences of men, so that no one with a good conscience could find fault with us. And this we do [[4:2|in the sight of God|coram Deo]], that is, by thinking of the divine presence and placing ourselves in the sight of God, who sees all things, with all reverence and guard of the heart.

paras.t: Quod si etiam opertum est Evangelium nostrum, id est, si prædicatio nostra de Christo aliquibus absconditur, ita ut eam non audiant, vel auditam non capiant; in his qui pereunt, id est in cordibus reproborum, est opertum, id est, occultatum est hoc modo: In quibus deus hujus sæculi, id est diabolus dominus impiorum (de quo ait Salvator: Venit princeps hujus mundi), excæcavit cooperative seu suggestive mentes infidelium. Vel: Deus hujus sæculi, id est Deus verus omnium sæculorum, hominumque malorum creator et Deus, excæcavit mentes, id est intellectus infidelium, permissive: quemadmodum dicitur Pharaonis cor indurasse. Unde et Christus in Evangelio: In judicium, inquit, ego in hunc mundum veni, ut qui non vident, videant; et qui vident, cæci fiant. Ut non fulgeat, id est innotescat, eis illuminatio Evangelii, id est evangelica doctrina, gloriæ, id est majestatis, Christi, qui est imago Dei, id est a Patre secundum rationem similitudinis genitus. Est enim a Patre procedens, eique similis et æqualis per omnia. Propter quod ipse ait: Qui videt me, videt et Patrem. Porro quod Christus sit imago Dei, hinc liquet:
paras.en: [[4:3|And if our gospel be also hid|Quod si etiam opertum est Evangelium nostrum]], that is, if our preaching about Christ is hidden from some, so that they do not hear it, or, having heard it, do not grasp it; [[4:3|to them that are lost|in his qui pereunt]], that is, in the hearts of the reprobate, [[4:3|it is hid|est opertum]], that is, it is concealed in this way: [[4:4|In whom the god of this world|In quibus deus hujus sæculi]], that is, the devil, the lord of the wicked (of whom the Saviour says: [[John 14:30|the prince of this world: cometh|Venit princeps hujus mundi]]), [[4:4|hath blinded|excæcavit]], by cooperating or suggesting, [[4:4|the minds of unbelievers|mentes infidelium]]. Or: *The God of this world*, that is, the true God of all ages[[1 Tim 1:17||]] [Latin *sæculum* is both "world" and "age"], the creator and God even of evil men, *hath blinded the minds*, that is, the understandings, *of unbelievers*, by permitting it: in the way in which he is said to have hardened Pharao's heart[[Ex 4:21||]][[Ex 7:3||]][[Ex 14:4||]] [the margin adds "etc."]. Hence Christ too says in the Gospel: [[John 9:39|For judgment|In judicium]], he says, [[John 9:39|I am come into this world: that they who see not may see; and they who see may become blind|ego in hunc mundum veni, ut qui non vident, videant; et qui vident, cæci fiant]]. so that there [[4:4|should not shine|Ut non fulgeat]], that is, be made known, [[4:4|unto them|eis]] [[4:4|the light of the gospel|illuminatio Evangelii]], that is, the gospel teaching, [[4:4|of the glory|gloriæ]], that is, of the majesty, [[4:4|of Christ, who is the image of God|Christi, qui est imago Dei]], that is, begotten of the Father by way of likeness. For he proceeds from the Father, and is like him and equal to him in all things. Because of which he himself says: [[John 14:9|he that seeth me seeth the Father also|Qui videt me, videt et Patrem]]. Moreover, that Christ is the image of God is clear from this:

paras.t: Non enim nosmetipsos prædicamus, quasi in nobis salus vestra consistat, sed Jesum Christum Dominum nostrum prædicamus esse omnium salvatorem; nos autem servos vestros esse prædicamus, hoc est, vobis servientes in exhibitione spiritualium alimentorum, parantes vobis mensam Domini, spiritualemque escam proponentes, per Jesum, id est ex commissione et per gratiam Christi, qui nobis hoc injunxit officium.
paras.en: [[4:5|For we preach not ourselves|Non enim nosmetipsos prædicamus]], as though your salvation lay in us, [[4:5|but Jesus Christ our Lord|sed Jesum Christum Dominum nostrum]]: we preach him to be the saviour of all; [[4:5|and ourselves your servants|nos autem servos vestros]] we preach ourselves to be, that is, serving you by setting before you spiritual food, preparing for you the table of the Lord and putting before you spiritual meat, [[4:5|through Jesus|per Jesum]], that is, by the commission and through the grace of Christ, who laid this office upon us.

paras.t: Quoniam Deus trinus, simplex atque omnipotens, qui dixit, id est, interiori verbo fecit, de tenebris, id est post tenebras, vel, De tenebris, id est de materia obscura, lucem sensibilem splendescere, id est inchoative oriri. Unde dicitur in Genesi: In principio creavit Deus cœlum et terram, et tenebræ erant super faciem abyssi; dixitque Deus, Fiat lux; et facta est lux. Ipse illuxit in cordibus nostris, id est, lumen fidei atque divinæ sapientiæ mentibus nostris infudit, ad illuminationem scientiæ claritatis Dei, id est ad hoc ut nos illuminemur ad cognoscendum claritatem, id est nobilitatem seu excellentiam Dei; vel, Ad illuminationem, etc., id est ad hoc ut alios doceamus de notitia claritatis Dei, id est perfectionis divinæ: illuminationem, inquam, scientiæ tendentis in faciem Jesu Christi, id est dirigentis nos ad veram Christi notitiam, qua eum agnoscimus esse Deum et hominem. Facies autem notitiam significat, quia per faciem unusquisque potissimum cognoscitur.
paras.en: [[4:6|For God|Quoniam Deus]], three, simple and almighty, [[4:6|who commanded|qui dixit]] [Latin *dixit*, "said"], that is, made by his inward word, [[4:6|out of darkness|de tenebris]], that is, after darkness, or, *out of darkness*, that is, out of dark matter, [[4:6|the light|lucem]] (sensible light) [[4:6|to shine|splendescere]], that is, to begin to rise. Hence it is said in Genesis: [[Gen 1:1|In the beginning God created heaven, and earth|In principio creavit Deus cœlum et terram]], and [[Gen 1:2|darkness was upon the face of the deep|tenebræ erant super faciem abyssi]]; [[Gen 1:3|And God said: Be light made. And light was made|dixitque Deus, Fiat lux; et facta est lux]] [the margin gives Gen. i, 1-3]. [[4:6|hath shined in our hearts|Ipse illuxit in cordibus nostris]], that is, has poured into our minds the light of faith and of divine wisdom, [[4:6|to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God|ad illuminationem scientiæ claritatis Dei]], that is, so that we may be enlightened to know the glory, that is, the nobility or excellence, of God; or, *to give the light*, etc., that is, so that we may teach others about the knowledge of the glory of God, that is, of the divine perfection: the light, I say, of a knowledge that tends [[4:6|in the face of Christ Jesus|in faciem Jesu Christi]] [Latin *in faciem*, "towards the face"], that is, that directs us to the true knowledge of Christ, by which we acknowledge him to be God and man. Now *face* signifies knowledge, because it is chiefly by the face that each one is known.

paras.t: Habemus autem thesaurum istum, id est gratiam tantæ illuminationis. Unde et Salomon: Thesaurus, inquit, desiderabilis in ore sapientis; et rursus: Pretiosior est sapientia cunctis opibus; et omnia quæ desiderantur, huic non valent comparari. In vasis fictilibus, id est corporibus fragilibus. Non quod corpus, quod est pars integralis hominis, sit hujus thesauri subjectum immediatum, sed animæ: quoniam tamen animæ subjectum est corpus, ideo nos in corpore peregrinantes, dicimur thesaurum istum habere in vasis fictilibus. Ut sublimitas, id est altitudo nostræ perfectionis in vita, in signis, in documentis, sit virtutis Dei, id est, Deo adscribatur, non nostræ fragilitati. Ideo additur: et non ex nobis, id est, non ex nostra naturali potestate oriri putetur.
paras.en: [[4:7|But we have this treasure|Habemus autem thesaurum istum]], that is, the grace of so great an enlightenment. Hence Solomon too says: [[Prov 21:20|There is a treasure|Thesaurus]], he says, [[Prov 21:20|to be desired|desiderabilis]] in the mouth of the wise [Denis reads *in ore sapientis*, "in the mouth of the wise"; the Vulgate has "and oil in the dwelling of the just"]; and again: wisdom [[Prov 3:15|is more precious than all riches: and all the things that are desired, are not to be compared to her|Pretiosior est sapientia cunctis opibus; et omnia quæ desiderantur, huic non valent comparari]]. [[4:7|in earthen vessels|In vasis fictilibus]], that is, in frail bodies. Not that the body, which is an integral part of man, is the immediate subject of this treasure, but rather the soul is; yet since the body is the subject of the soul [that is, the body is what the soul informs and dwells in], we, while we are pilgrims in the body, are said to have this treasure in earthen vessels. [[4:7|that the excellency|Ut sublimitas]], that is, the height of our perfection in life, in signs, in teachings, [[4:7|may be of the power of God|sit virtutis Dei]], that is, may be ascribed to God, not to our frailty. Therefore he adds: [[4:7|and not of us|et non ex nobis]], that is, let it not be thought to arise from our natural power.

paras.t: In omnibus, loco, causa et tempore, saltem in genere, tribulationem patimur propter justitiam; sed non angustiamur, id est, non opprimimur mente, quia de Dei auxilio certi sumus. Aporiamur, id est, temporalibus bonis privamur et pauperes sumus; sed non destituimur, id est, non caremus spiritualibus verisque divitiis: imo in his tanto magis abundamus, quanto in illis pauperiores propter Christum sumus. Etenim beati pauperes, quoniam ipsorum est regnum cœlorum. Persecutionem, id est de loco ad locum fugationem, patimur; sed non derelinquimur a Deo. Dejicimur, id est conculcamur; sed non perimus, quoniam liberamur semper a Domino corporaliter aut spiritualiter, et interim utroque modo.
paras.en: [[4:8|In all things|In omnibus]], in place, cause and time, at least in kind, [[4:8|we suffer tribulation|tribulationem patimur]] for justice' sake; [[4:8|but are not distressed|sed non angustiamur]], that is, we are not crushed in mind, for we are sure of God's help. [[4:8|We are straitened|Aporiamur]] [Latin *aporiamur*, from the Greek, "we are at a loss"], that is, we are deprived of temporal goods and are poor; [[4:8|but are not destitute|sed non destituimur]], that is, we do not lack spiritual and true riches: nay, in these we abound all the more, the poorer we are in the others for Christ's sake. For [[Matt 5:3|Blessed are the poor|beati pauperes]], [[Matt 5:3|for theirs is the kingdom of heaven|quoniam ipsorum est regnum cœlorum]]. [[4:9|We suffer|patimur]] [[4:9|persecution|Persecutionem]], that is, being driven from place to place; [[4:9|but are not forsaken|sed non derelinquimur]] by God. [[4:9|We are cast down|Dejicimur]], that is, we are trampled on; [[4:9|but we perish not|sed non perimus]], for we are always delivered by the Lord, bodily or spiritually, and sometimes in both ways.

paras.t: Semper mortificationem Jesu, id est passionem dominicam, in corpore nostro circumferentes, per cruciformem imitationem et corporis quotidianam flagellationem. Unde alibi dicit Apostolus: In omni fiducia magnificabitur Christus in corpore meo, sive per vitam, sive per mortem; item, Ego stigmata Domini Jesu in corpore meo porto. Ut et vita Jesu, id est conversatio quam habuit in hoc mundo, in corporibus nostris manifestetur, id est, Christi vestigia in agendo sectemur; vel, Vita Jesu immortalis quam nunc habet, in corporibus nostris manifestetur in resurrectione futura, quando reformabit corpus humilitatis nostræ configuratum corpori claritatis suæ.
paras.en: [[4:10|Always|Semper]] [[4:10|the mortification of Jesus|mortificationem Jesu]], that is, the Lord's passion, [[4:10|bearing about in our body|in corpore nostro circumferentes]], by imitating the cross and by the daily scourging of the body. Hence the Apostle says elsewhere: [[Phil 1:20|with all confidence|In omni fiducia]] [[Phil 1:20|shall Christ be magnified in my body, whether it be by life or by death|magnificabitur Christus in corpore meo, sive per vitam, sive per mortem]]; and again, [[Gal 6:17|I bear the marks of the Lord Jesus in my body|Ego stigmata Domini Jesu in corpore meo porto]]. [[4:10|that the life also of Jesus|Ut et vita Jesu]], that is, the manner of life he led in this world, [[4:10|may be made manifest in our bodies|in corporibus nostris manifestetur]], that is, that we may follow Christ's footsteps in what we do; or, may the immortal life of Jesus, which he now has, be made manifest in our bodies in the resurrection to come, when he [[Phil 3:21|will reform the body of our lowness, made like to the body of his glory|reformabit corpus humilitatis nostræ configuratum corpori claritatis suæ]].

paras.t: Semper enim, id est in omni differentia temporis in genere, nos Apostoli et alii successores nostri, qui vivimus nunc in vita naturæ et gratiæ, in mortem tradimur, id est, periculis mortis afficimur, propter Jesum, id est ejus amore, et propter prædicationem evangelicæ veritatis: sicut et Christus prædixit, Venit hora ut omnis qui interficit vos, arbitretur obsequium se præstare Deo; et denuo, Eritis odio omnibus hominibus propter Filium hominis; ut et vita Jesu, quam habet jam immortalis, manifestetur in carne nostra mortali, id est, gloria immortalitatis nostræ carni præstetur, quando corruptibile hoc induet incorruptionem, et mortale hoc immortalitatem.
paras.en: [[4:11|For|enim]] [[4:11|always|Semper]], that is, at every distinction of time, in kind, [[4:11|we|nos]] Apostles and our other successors, [[4:11|who live|qui vivimus]] now in the life of nature and of grace, are [[4:11|delivered unto death|in mortem tradimur]], that is, are beset by dangers of death, [[4:11|for Jesus' sake|propter Jesum]], that is, for love of him and for the preaching of the gospel truth: as Christ also foretold: [[John 16:2|the hour cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doth a service to God|Venit hora ut omnis qui interficit vos, arbitretur obsequium se præstare Deo]]; and again, [[Matt 10:22|you shall be hated by all men|Eritis odio omnibus hominibus]] for the sake of the Son of man[[Matt 24:9||]] [the margin gives Matt. x [22] and xxiv, 9; Denis's "for the Son of man" is the wording of Luke 6:22]; [[4:11|that the life also of Jesus|ut et vita Jesu]], which he now has immortal, [[4:11|may be made manifest in our mortal flesh|manifestetur in carne nostra mortali]], that is, that the glory of immortality may be bestowed on our flesh, when [[1 Cor 15:53|this corruptible must put on incorruption: and this mortal must put on immortality|corruptibile hoc induet incorruptionem, et mortale hoc immortalitatem]].

paras.t: Ergo mors, id est passio Christi, in nobis operatur, id est, fructuosa est nobis, excitando nos ad sui imitationem. Vita autem naturæ seu culpæ, operatur in vobis qui Christi vestigia imitari negligitis; vel, Vita gratiæ, scilicet fides et caritas, operatur in vobis opera meritoria: quia per hoc quod nos taliter mortificamur, vos ad Deum convertimini, et vivitis coram illo.
paras.en: [[4:12|So then death|Ergo mors]], that is, the passion of Christ, [[4:12|worketh in us|in nobis operatur]], that is, is fruitful for us, by stirring us to imitate it. [[4:12|but life|Vita autem]] of nature or of sin works [[4:12|in you|in vobis]] who neglect to follow the footsteps of Christ; or, the life of grace, namely faith and charity, works meritorious works in you: because through our being mortified in this way, you are converted to God and live before him.

paras.t: Consequenter ostendit eamdem fuisse fidem in populo utriusque Testamenti, tractatque de diversis effectibus, meritis et actibus fidei. Habentes autem nos novi Testamenti ministri eumdem spiritum fidei, id est Spiritum Sanctum fidei datorem, quem habuerunt Sancti antiqui. Vel per spiritum fidei, intelligenda est ipsa fides, vel gratia seu motio fidei, quæ una et eadem est in his qui ante Christi adventum fuerunt, et in posterioribus, quamvis sit modo magis explicita. Sicut scriptum est in libro Psalmorum a David propheta: Credidi corde, propter quod locutus sum ore verba fidelis confessionis. Confessio namque ista est actus fidei. Unde alibi dictum est: Corde creditur ad justitiam, ore autem confessio fit ad salutem. Et nos credimus ea quæ illi, propter quod et loquimur fidem catholicam, confitendo ac prædicando; scientes fide certissima, quoniam Deus Pater seu Trinitas, qui suscitavit Jesum occisum a morte, et nos electos cum Jesu, id est sicut et Jesum, vel ad hoc ut simus cum Jesu in regno, suscitabit in die novissimo, et constituet nos vobiscum ad dexteram in patria, ubi agni ponentur.
paras.en: Next he shows that the faith was the same in the people of both Testaments, and treats of the various effects, merits and acts of faith. [[4:13|But having|Habentes autem]] (we, ministers of the new Testament) [[4:13|the same spirit of faith|eumdem spiritum fidei]], that is, the Holy Ghost, the giver of faith, whom the holy men of old had. Or by *the spirit of faith* is to be understood faith itself, or the grace or movement of faith, which is one and the same in those who lived before Christ's coming and in those after, although it is now more explicit. [[4:13|as it is written|Sicut scriptum est]] in the book of Psalms by David the prophet: [[4:13|I believed|Credidi]] with the heart, [[4:13|for which cause I have spoken|propter quod locutus sum]] with the mouth the words of faithful confession[[Ps 115:1||]] [the margin gives Ps. cxv, 10, the Hebrew numbering; in the Vulgate it is Ps 115:1]. For that confession is an act of faith. Hence it is said elsewhere: [[Rom 10:10|with the heart, we believe unto justice: but, with the mouth, confession is made unto salvation|Corde creditur ad justitiam, ore autem confessio fit ad salutem]]. [[4:13|we also believe|Et nos credimus]] what they believed, [[4:13|For which cause we speak also|propter quod et loquimur]] the catholic faith, by confessing and preaching it; [[4:14|Knowing|scientes]] by most certain faith [[4:14|that he|quoniam]] (God the Father, or the Trinity) [[4:14|who raised up Jesus|qui suscitavit Jesum]], slain, from death, and us, the elect, [[4:14|also with Jesus|electos cum Jesu]], that is, as he raised Jesus, or so that we may be with Jesus in the kingdom, [[4:14|will raise us up|suscitabit]] on the last day, [[4:14|and place us with you|et constituet nos vobiscum]] at the right hand in our true country, where the lambs shall be placed[[Matt 25:33||]].

paras.t: Omnia enim propter vos, id est, universa ministeria nostra ad vestram ordinantur salutem, ut gratia Dei abundans per multos, id est ab uno transfusa seu ministrata in alium: secundum quod Petrus hortatur, Unusquisque sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes; in gratiarum actione abundet, id est, cum gratiarum actione copiose referatur et ordinetur seu reducatur ad suum principium, scilicet Deum […] quatenus omnes Deo gratias referant, et omne charisma gratiæ illi tribuant.
paras.en: [[4:15|For all things are for your sakes|Omnia enim propter vos]], that is, all our ministries are ordered to your salvation, [[4:15|that the grace|ut gratia]] of God, [[4:15|abounding through many|abundans per multos]], that is, passed on or ministered from one to another: as Peter exhorts, [[1 Pet 4:10|As every man hath received grace, ministering the same one to another|Unusquisque sicut accepit gratiam, in alterutrum illam administrantes]] [no margin reference here; the words are 1 Pet 4:10]; [[4:15|may abound in thanksgiving|in gratiarum actione abundet]], that is, may with thanksgiving be abundantly referred and ordered, or led back, to its source, namely God […] so that all may give thanks to God and ascribe to him every gift [Latin *charisma*] of grace.

paras.t: Propter quod prosequendum, videlicet ut Deo gratiæ referantur, non deficimus in adversis, nec fatigamur in opere bono, nec cessamus, quoniam sola perseverantia coronatur. Sed licet is qui foris est, noster homo, id est caro nostra mortalis, in qua est humana effigies qua homines esse cognoscimur, corrumpatur, quotidie tendendo ad mortem, et sustinendo læsuras ac plagas; tamen is qui intus est, id est anima nostra, in qua est summæ Trinitatis imago, renovatur, recipiendo nova lumina gratiarum, reflorendo in Dei cognitione, ascendendo in divino amore, de die in diem, id est assidue, dum spiritualiter crescimus atque proficimus. Hoc autem dicitur, non quasi in nobis sint duo homines, sed propter distinctionem essentialium partium hominis.
paras.en: [[4:16|For which cause|Propter quod]], which we are to pursue, namely that thanks be given to God, [[4:16|we faint not|non deficimus]] in adversity, nor grow weary in good works, nor cease, since perseverance alone is crowned[[Matt 10:22||]]. [[4:16|but though our outward man|Sed licet is qui foris est, noster homo]], that is, our mortal flesh, in which is the human form by which we are known to be men, [[4:16|is corrupted|corrumpatur]], tending daily towards death and bearing hurts and wounds; [[4:16|yet the inward man|tamen is qui intus est]], that is, our soul, in which is the image of the most high Trinity, [[4:16|is renewed|renovatur]], by receiving new lights of graces, by flowering again in the knowledge of God, by rising in divine love, [[4:16|day by day|de die in diem]], that is, constantly, while we grow and advance spiritually. This is said, not as though there were two men in us, but because of the distinction of the essential parts of man.

paras.t: Id enim quod in præsenti exsilio seu tempore est momentaneum et leve tribulationis nostræ, id est tribulatio ista levis atque brevissima (comparatione futuræ jucunditatis ac æternitatis) quam patimur jam, supra modum, id est ultra condignum et capacitatem nostri intellectus, in sublimitate, id est in regno cœlesti, vel in liberalitate bonitatis divinæ, æternum gloriæ pondus, id est perpetuam felicitatis mensuram: de qua ait Salvator, Mensuram bonam et confertam et coagitatam et superefluentem dabunt in sinum vestrum; operatur, id est, meretur et efficit, in nobis, nunc per spem, postmodum vero in re, non contemplantibus nobis, id est, quia non principaliter adspicimus, nec finaliter intuemur, quæ videntur, id est visibilia et terrena, sed quæ non videntur, id est bona supercœlestia, quæ oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit. Quæ enim videntur a nobis oculo corporali, temporalia sunt, id est transitoria et caduca; quæ autem non videntur, id est spiritualia bona nobis præparata in regno, æterna sunt essentialiter vel participative.
paras.en: [[4:17|For that which is at present|Id enim quod in præsenti]] exile or time [[4:17|momentary and light of our tribulation|est momentaneum et leve tribulationis nostræ]], that is, this tribulation, light and very brief (in comparison with the joy and eternity to come), which we now suffer, [[4:17|above measure|supra modum]], that is, beyond what is condign and beyond the capacity of our understanding, [[4:17|exceedingly|in sublimitate]] [Latin *in sublimitate*, "in the height"], that is, in the heavenly kingdom, or in the liberality of the divine goodness, [[4:17|an eternal weight of glory|æternum gloriæ pondus]], that is, an everlasting measure of happiness: of which the Saviour says: [[Luke 6:38|good measure and pressed down and shaken together and running over shall they give into your bosom|Mensuram bonam et confertam et coagitatam et superefluentem dabunt in sinum vestrum]]; [[4:17|worketh|operatur]], that is, merits and brings about, [[4:17|for us|in nobis]], now in hope, but afterwards in fact, [[4:18|While we look not|non contemplantibus nobis]], that is, because we do not look chiefly at, nor gaze as at our end upon, [[4:18|at the things which are seen|quæ videntur]], that is, visible and earthly things, [[4:18|but at the things which are not seen|sed quæ non videntur]], that is, the goods above the heavens, which [[1 Cor 2:9|eye hath not seen, nor ear heard|oculus non vidit, nec auris audivit]]. [[4:18|For the things which are seen|Quæ enim videntur]] by us with the bodily eye [[4:18|are temporal|temporalia sunt]], that is, passing and perishable; [[4:18|but the things which are not seen|quæ autem non videntur]], that is, the spiritual goods prepared for us in the kingdom, [[4:18|are eternal|æterna sunt]] essentially or by participation.

10.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI DECIMI : IPSE AUTEM EGO PAULUS, ETC.
10.title_en: Exposition of the tenth chapter: Now I Paul myself, etc.

paras.t: FACTA exhortatione ad bonos, jam sermo dirigitur ad incorrectos, qui adhuc pseudoapostolis adhæserunt : qui multa vitia imposuerunt Apostolo, de quibus se consequenter excusat, sicut patebit. Ait ergo : Ipse autem ego Paulus obsecro, id est, per sacra rogo, vos, scilicet per mansuetudinem, id est mititatem, quæ iram refrenat, et modestiam, id est moderamen seu discretionem, Christi : qui per Jeremiam ait, Ego quasi agnus mansuetus qui portatur ad victimam; et iterum, Discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde ; qui in facie quidem, id est in præsentia vestra, sive exterius, humilis sum inter vos exsistens, quasi blandiens vobis, sicut pseudoapostoli mihi imponunt, absens autem a vobis confido in vobis, id est, fiducialiter, audacter et dure redarguo vos, quia non timeo mihi mala inferri a vobis dum absens sum, quemadmodum præsens. Imposuerunt autem Apostolo quod esset carnalis, quoniam more carnalium, præsens exsistens, dulcis et blandus esset in verbis, quasi timens periculum si durius ageret, absens vero rigidus foret.
paras.en: Having made his exhortation to the good, he now turns his words to the uncorrected, who still clung to the false apostles: these laid many faults to the Apostle's charge, of which he then clears himself, as will appear. He says therefore: [[10:1|Now I Paul, myself beseech|Ipse autem ego Paulus obsecro]], that is, I entreat by holy things, [[10:1|you|vos]], namely [[10:1|by the mildness|per mansuetudinem]], that is, gentleness, which bridles anger, [[10:1|and modesty|et modestiam]], that is, moderation or discretion, [[10:1|of Christ|Christi]]: who says by Jeremias, [[Jer 11:19|I was as a meek lamb, that is carried to be a victim|Ego quasi agnus mansuetus qui portatur ad victimam]]; and again, [[Matt 11:29|learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart|Discite a me quia mitis sum et humilis corde]]; [[10:1|who in presence indeed|qui in facie quidem]], that is, in your presence, or outwardly, [[10:1|am lowly among you|humilis sum inter vos]], being as it were one who flatters you, as the false apostles charge against me, [[10:1|but being absent|absens autem]] from you [[10:1|am bold toward you|confido in vobis]], that is, I rebuke you confidently, boldly and harshly, because I do not fear that harm will be done me by you while I am absent, as I would when present. For they charged the Apostle with being carnal, since in the manner of carnal men, when present he was sweet and smooth in his words, as though fearing danger if he dealt more harshly, but when absent he was severe.

paras.t: Rogo autem vos, ne sic sentiatis de me, ne præsens, id est apud vos exsistens, audeam, id est, audacter me habeam, incorrectos durissime increpando, per eam confidentiam, id est fiduciam illam imperterritam, qua existimor ab æmulis audere, id est audacter invehere, in quosdam, id est incorrectos a pseudoapostolis deceptos, quum absens sum, qui incorrecti arbitrantur nos tanquam secundum carnem ambulemus, id est, carnaliter conversari, et in temporalibus finem nos constituere existimant : qui utique errant.
paras.en: [[10:2|But I beseech you|Rogo autem vos]], not to think thus of me, [[10:2|that I may not be bold when I am present|ne præsens audeam]], that is, when among you, be bold, that is, bear myself boldly, rebuking the uncorrected most harshly, [[10:2|with that confidence|per eam confidentiam]], that is, that undaunted assurance, [[10:2|wherewith I am thought to be bold|qua existimor audere]] by my rivals, that is, to inveigh boldly, [[10:2|against some|in quosdam]], that is, the uncorrected deceived by the false apostles, when I am absent; [[10:2|who reckon us as if we walked according to the flesh|qui arbitrantur nos tamquam secundum carnem ambulemus]]: these uncorrected think that we live carnally and set our end in temporal things: and they are certainly mistaken.

paras.t: In carne enim ambulantes, id est in hac corruptibili carne viventes et peregrinantes, non secundum carnem militamus, id est, non carnaliter exercemur ad prælium contra adversarios humanæ salutis. Militia quippe est vita hominis super terram ; sed militia nostra spiritualis est, et triumphum spiritualem intendit. Nam arma militiæ nostræ, quibus prædicando et conversando contra dæmones et perversos homines dimicamus, videlicet virtutes et dona Spiritus Sancti, non carnalia sunt, nec humana virtute adepta, sed potentia Deo, id est Dei virtute efficacia, ad destructionem munitionum, id est virium quibus dæmones et impii homines contra fidei veritatem armantur; consilia impiorum destruentes nostra prædicatione et miraculorum operatione ; et omnem altitudinem, id est præsumptionem ac profunditatem mundanæ et naturalis sapientiæ, extollentem se adversus scientiam Dei, id est theologicæ veritati seu fidei assertionibus contradicentem, destruentes seu reprobantes. Hoc fecit Apostolus Athenis, disputando contra philosophos. Et in captivitatem redigentes, id est, captivantes, et nostræ doctrinæ ac fidei jugo subdentes, omnem intellectum, id est mentem quorumdam de omni genere hominum, in obsequium Christi, id est ad hoc ut Christo deserviant, ejusque auctoritati potius quam humanæ rationi adhæreant. Convertit enim Apostolus quosdam doctos, et quosdam indoctos ; sicque de ceteris generibus hominum quosdam convertit ad Christum : et sic quoque omnium intellectum subjecit fidei præceptisque Christi, quatenus incomprehensibilia credant, et Deo in cunctis obediant.
paras.en: [[10:3|For though we walk in the flesh|In carne enim ambulantes]], that is, living and journeying as pilgrims in this corruptible flesh, [[10:3|we do not war according to the flesh|non secundum carnem militamus]], that is, we are not trained carnally for battle against the adversaries of human salvation. For [[Job 7:1|The life of man upon earth is a warfare|Militia quippe est vita hominis super terram]]; but our warfare is spiritual, and aims at a spiritual triumph. [[10:4|For the weapons of our warfare|Nam arma militiæ nostræ]], with which by preaching and by our manner of life we fight against demons and perverse men, namely the virtues and gifts of the Holy Ghost, [[10:4|are not carnal|non carnalia sunt]], nor gained by human power, [[10:4|but mighty to God|sed potentia Deo]], that is, effective by the power of God, [[10:4|unto the pulling down of fortifications|ad destructionem munitionum]], that is, of the forces with which demons and wicked men arm themselves against the truth of the faith; [[10:4|destroying counsels|consilia destruentes]] of the wicked by our preaching and the working of miracles; [[10:5|And every height|et omnem altitudinem]], that is, the presumption and depth of worldly and natural wisdom, [[10:5|that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God|extollentem se adversus scientiam Dei]], that is, contradicting theological truth or the assertions of the faith, destroying, or confuting. This the Apostle did at Athens, disputing against the philosophers[[Acts 17:16||]]. [[10:5|and bringing into captivity|Et in captivitatem redigentes]], that is, taking captive and subjecting to the yoke of our teaching and faith, [[10:5|every understanding|omnem intellectum]], that is, the minds of some of every kind of men, [[10:5|unto the obedience of Christ|in obsequium Christi]], that is, so that they may serve Christ and adhere to his authority rather than to human reason. For the Apostle converted some learned and some unlearned; and so of the other kinds of men he converted some to Christ: and thus too he subjected the understanding of all to the faith and precepts of Christ, so that they believe things incomprehensible and obey God in all things.

paras.t: Et in promptu habentes, id est, expedite potentes, ulcisci omnem inobedientiam, tradendo excommunicatos et impios Satanæ in interitum carnis, vel, Christum invocando possumus de eis ultionem acquirere, quum impleta fuerit vestra obedientia, id est, perfectam esse noverimus vestram obedientiam. Tunc enim et non ante, decet nos contra rebelles insurgere, quoniam prius confirmandi sunt boni, quam mali torquendi. Ad quod pertinere potest illud Apocalypsis : Nolite nocere terræ et mari, neque arboribus, quoadusque signemus servos Dei nostri in frontibus eorum.
paras.en: [[10:6|And having in readiness|Et in promptu habentes]], that is, being readily able, [[10:6|to revenge all disobedience|ulcisci omnem inobedientiam]], by delivering the excommunicated and wicked to Satan for the destruction of the flesh[[1 Cor 5:5||]]; or, by calling upon Christ we can obtain vengeance on them; [[10:6|when your obedience shall be fulfilled|quum impleta fuerit vestra obedientia]], that is, when we know your obedience to be perfect. For then and not before it befits us to rise against the rebellious, since the good must be strengthened before the wicked are punished. To this may belong that word of the Apocalypse: [[Apoc 7:3|Hurt not the earth nor the sea nor the trees, till we sign the servants of our God in their foreheads|Nolite nocere terræ et mari, neque arboribus, quoadusque signemus servos Dei nostri in frontibus eorum]].

paras.t: Quæ secundum faciem sunt, videte : id est, si prædicta spiritualia quibus ostendi me esse verum Christi apostolum et falsis præferendum, non vobis sufficiunt, quæ secundum faciem sunt, id est, manifeste apparent in illis et in me, videte, id est pensate. Si quis illorum pseudoapostolorum confidit sibi, id est, de propria perfectione præsumit, Christi se esse, id est ad Christum per gratiam se pertinere, hoc cogitet iterum apud se, id est, diligenter consideret atque revolvat, ne se præferat nobis ; quia sicut ipse Christi est, secundum opinionem suam fallacem, ita et nos Christi sumus fideles ministri, secundum veritatem.
paras.en: [[10:7|See the things that are according to outward appearance|Quæ secundum faciem sunt, videte]]: that is, if the spiritual things aforesaid, by which I have shown that I am a true apostle of Christ and to be preferred to the false, are not enough for you, the things that are according to appearance, that is, that plainly appear in them and in me, see, that is, weigh. [[10:7|If any man|Si quis]] of those false apostles [[10:7|trust to himself|confidit sibi]], that is, presumes on his own perfection, [[10:7|that he is Christ's|Christi se esse]], that is, that he belongs to Christ by grace, [[10:7|let him think this again with himself|hoc cogitet iterum apud se]], that is, let him carefully consider and turn it over, lest he prefer himself to us; [[10:7|that as he is Christ's|quia sicut ipse Christi est]], according to his own false opinion, [[10:7|so are we also|ita et nos]] faithful ministers of Christ, according to the truth.

paras.t: Nam et si amplius aliquid gloriatus fuero in Domino de potestate nostra, quam illi de sua gloriari possunt, id est, quamvis illis nostram potestatem prætulero, quam dedit nobis Dominus in ædificationem, et non in destructionem, id est ad hoc ut ea salubriter utamur, non impie abutamur, videlicet ut vos verbis atque exemplis ædificemus in vita spirituali, et non inficiamus nec subvertamus quempiam vestrum ; non erubescam quasi præsumptuose hoc agens, quia sic est. Verumtamen ministri Christi potestate sibi concessa abuti possunt, et sæpius abutuntur, ut patet de malis sacerdotibus, sed non sine grandi peccato.
paras.en: [[10:8|For if also I should boast somewhat more|Nam et si amplius aliquid gloriatus fuero]] in the Lord [[10:8|of our power|de potestate nostra]] than they can glory of theirs, that is, even though I should prefer our power to theirs, [[10:8|which the Lord hath given us unto edification|quam dedit nobis Dominus in ædificationem]], and not for destruction, that is, so that we may use it to salvation, not wickedly abuse it, namely that we may build you up in the spiritual life by words and examples, and not infect or overthrow any of you; [[10:8|I should not be ashamed|non erubescam]], as though doing this presumptuously, because it is so. Yet the ministers of Christ can abuse the power granted them, and quite often do, as is plain of bad priests, but not without grave sin.

paras.t: Denique, ne isti erronei æstimarent Apostolum non esse facturum quum præsens adesset, quod absens minabatur, dicendo se potentem et promptum ulcisci omnem inobedientiam : ne igitur ita sentirent, adjunxit : Ut autem non existimer ab incorrectis et falsis, tanquam terrere vos per epistolas, id est in epistolis meis ad vos missis verba minatoria miscere, quæ non audebo præsens implere (nam hoc mihi imponunt) ; quoniam quidem epistolæ meæ, inquiunt illi detractores, graves sunt et fortes, id est minaces, et intellectu difficiles, atque verbosæ, præsentia autem corporis infirma, id est, nos ipsi corporaliter præsentes, impotentes et timidi sumus, non audentes exercere rigorem, sed adulantes, et sermo noster contemptibilis, id est non rhetoricus, nec humanis argumentis firmatus, sed simplex et nudus, nil probans ; hoc cogitet qui ejusmodi est, id est qui talia nobis imponit, quia quales sumus verbo per epistolas, id est in epistolis, dum sumus absentes, tales erimus et præsentes, in facto, id est, opere exsequemur quæcumque minamur, et nos facturos prædicimus in epistolis vobis transmissis.
paras.en: Further, lest these erring men should think that the Apostle would not do when present what he threatened when absent, saying that he was able and ready to revenge all disobedience: lest, then, they should think so, he added: [[10:9|But that I may not be thought|Ut autem non existimer]] by the uncorrected and false, [[10:9|as it were to terrify you by epistles|tanquam terrere vos per epistolas]], that is, to mingle threatening words in my letters sent to you, which I will not dare to fulfil when present (for this they charge against me); [[10:10|For his epistles indeed|quoniam quidem epistolæ]] (my epistles), [[10:10|say they|inquiunt]], those detractors, [[10:10|are weighty and strong|graves sunt et fortes]], that is, threatening, and hard to understand, and wordy, [[10:10|but his bodily presence is weak|præsentia autem corporis infirma]], that is, we ourselves, bodily present, are powerless and timid, not daring to use severity, but flattering, [[10:10|and his speech contemptible|et sermo contemptibilis]] (our speech), that is, not rhetorical, nor supported by human arguments, but simple and bare, proving nothing; [[10:11|Let such a one think this|hoc cogitet qui ejusmodi est]], that is, he who lays such things to our charge, [[10:11|that such as we are in word by epistles|quia quales sumus verbo per epistolas]], that is, in epistles, while we are [[10:11|when absent|absentes]], [[10:11|such also we will be indeed when present|tales erimus et præsentes, in facto]], that is, we will carry out in deed whatever we threaten and foretell that we will do in the epistles sent to you.

paras.t: Non enim audemus salva conscientia, inserere, id est connumerare, aut comparare, id est vere pares asserere, nos, quibusdam qui semetipsos commendant ob propriam laudem et aliorum deceptionem, videlicet ambitiosis et pseudoapostolis, qui potestatem sibi usurpant, et delinquentium vitia palpant. Si enim diceremus nos eis pares aut similes, mentiremur. Sed nos ipsi in nobis, id est in consideratione et examine mentis nostræ, sumus nosmetipsos metientes seu mensurantes, id est, nos ipsos diligenter discutimus, gratiamque nobis collatam perpendimus, ne præfixos nobis terminos transgrediamur, et plus justo nos ipsos jactemus, et sumus comparantes nosmetipsos nobis, id est, moderate et sobrie de nobis sentimus, propriamque mensuram pensamus.
paras.en: [[10:12|For we dare not match|Non enim audemus inserere]] with a safe conscience, that is, number ourselves among, [[10:12|or compare ourselves with some|aut comparare nos quibusdam]], that is, truly declare ourselves equal, [[10:12|that commend themselves|qui seipsos commendant]] for their own praise and the deceiving of others, namely the ambitious and the false apostles, who usurp power to themselves and stroke [that is, flatter and pass over] the vices of offenders. For if we said we were equal or like to them, we should lie. [[10:12|but we measure ourselves by ourselves|sed ipsi in nobis nosmetipsos metientes]], that is, in the consideration and examination of our mind we measure ourselves, that is, we examine ourselves carefully and weigh the grace bestowed on us, lest we pass the bounds set for us and boast of ourselves more than is just; [[10:12|and compare ourselves with ourselves|et comparantes nosmetipsos nobis]], that is, we think of ourselves with moderation and sobriety, and weigh our own measure.

paras.t: Nos autem non in immensum gloriabimur, id est, ultra terminum nobis divinitus præstitutum nihil præsumimus, sed gloriamur, et gloriando exercemus nostræ prædicationis officium, secundum mensuram regulæ, id est secundum extensionem ordinationis divinæ, quæ omnium rerum prima regula est; quam mensuram seu extensionem mensus est nobis Deus, id est, perambulandam præfixit sapientia Dei : cujus nutu missi sunt singuli Apostolorum ad certas determinatasque gentes, de quarum conversione gloriarentur in Domino. Ideo subditur : mensuram pertingendi usque ad vos : quia ex divina revelatione perrexit Apostolus Corinthum.
paras.en: [[10:13|But we will not glory beyond our measure|Nos autem non in immensum gloriabimur]], that is, we presume nothing beyond the bound divinely set for us; [[10:13|but|sed]] we glory, and in glorying exercise the office of our preaching, [[10:13|according to the measure of the rule|secundum mensuram regulæ]], that is, according to the extent of the divine ordinance, which is the first rule of all things; [[10:13|which God hath measured to us|qua mensus est nobis Deus]], which measure or extent the wisdom of God has appointed for us to travel through: by whose will each of the Apostles was sent to certain fixed nations, of whose conversion they might glory in the Lord. Therefore it is added: [[10:13|a measure to reach even unto you|mensuram pertingendi usque ad vos]]: for by divine revelation the Apostle went to Corinth.

paras.t: Non enim quasi non pertingentes ad vos, ad quorum conversionem destinati sumus, superextendimus nos, id est, ultra præscriptum a Deo terminum non tendimus. Usque ad vos enim pervenimus in Evangelio Christi, id est in prædicatione evangelica. Non tamen dumtaxat usque ad Corinthum venit, quippe qui ad Illyricum mare per circuitum Evangelium Christi replevit.
paras.en: [[10:14|For we stretch not ourselves beyond our measure, as if we reached not unto you|Non enim quasi non pertingentes ad vos, superextendimus nos]], to whose conversion we were appointed: that is, we do not reach beyond the bound prescribed by God.
